fields.why: "356 (87%) occurred in passengers and 54 (13%) in crew members" is the make-up of one case group, with no group denominators or outcome compared across groups; the epidemic curve by voyage is a description, not a contrast.
Follows from the above: no outcome is compared between passengers and crew or across voyages, and the ≥2% threshold only triggers the investigation, so it is not an analytic referent.

The report investigates one shipboard outbreak; surveillance (VSP/MIDRS) detected it and tracked cases. B's added surveillance/descriptive is defensible from "VSP used surveillance data", but outbreak investigation alone describes the design better.

One cruise ship arriving at a U.S. port is not national data or a nationwide sample, so B's 'US national' misreads "United States Jurisdiction"; the brief has no value for a single site outside state geography (the ship also sailed in Europe), so subnational is the closest fit.

brief_issues: setting has no value for a single facility or vessel not tied to a state (e.g. a cruise ship under U.S. jurisdiction); a rule mapping single sites to 'US subnational' would settle it. The brief could also say that a case breakdown by group with no denominators is a summary, not a comparison.
